title: Measuring Protein Interactions in Mammalian Cells Using Bioluminescence Resonance Energy Transfer
author: Duval, Steffen, et al.

steps.title: Prepare expression vectors
steps.instruction: Generate mammalian expression vectors encoding the donor (RLuc8‑K‑RasG12V) and acceptor (GFP2‑K‑RasG12V) constructs; optimize to retain biological activity.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and verify reader
steps.instruction: Prepare cell‑culture medium and coelenterazine 400a substrate; confirm that the fluorescence/luminescence microplate reader can define three BRET‑pair channels (acceptor excitation 405 ± 10 nm, emission 515 ± 10 nm; donor emission 410 ± 40 nm; BRET emission 515 ± 40 nm) and has an injector for microliter substrate dispensing (e.g., CLARIOstar).

steps.title: Seed and prepare cells for transfection
steps.instruction: Plate HEK293‑EBNA cells in a 12‑well plate and grow to 50‑60 % confluence before transfection.

steps.title: Dilute plasmid stocks
steps.instruction: Dilute all plasmid stocks to 100 ng/µL.

steps.title: Assemble DNA mix per well
steps.instruction: For each well, total DNA = 1025 ng. Use Table 1 to determine the volume (µL) of each plasmid (from 100 ng/µL stock) required for the desired acceptor/donor (A/D) ratio; include a donor‑only control (BRET‑control). Place the calculated DNA volumes into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Prepare jetPRIME transfection mix
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL jetPRIME buffer to the DNA in the tube and vortex for 10 s. Vortex jetPRIME reagent for 1–2 s, spin down 5 s at 2000 × g, then add jetPRIME reagent at a 1:3 ratio per µg DNA (for 1025 ng DNA add 3 µL).

steps.title: Incubate transfection complex
steps.instruction: Incubate the DNA‑jetPRIME mixture at 22–25 °C without shaking for 10–15 min.

steps.title: Add DNA mix to cells
steps.instruction: Add the transfection mixture dropwise to the corresponding well.

steps.title: Incubate transfected cells
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator for up to 48 h to allow BRET‑biosensor expression.

steps.title: Optional drug treatment
steps.instruction: At 24 h post‑transfection, treat selected wells with 5 µM mevastatin in vehicle (0.1 % DMSO/ growth medium) for up to an additional 24 h.

steps.title: Export and merge raw signals
steps.instruction: Export raw luminescence/fluorescence signals for the acceptor, donor, and BRET channels from the plate reader and merge them into a single Excel workbook.

steps.title: Calculate raw BRET ratios
steps.instruction: For each well, compute (BRET‑channel / donor‑channel) for donor + acceptor samples, subtract the same ratio obtained from donor‑only control wells; this yields the raw BRET ratio.

steps.title: Average BRET ratios
steps.instruction: Average the raw BRET ratios across the quadruplicate technical repeats for each sample.

steps.title: Compute expression signal ratios
steps.instruction: For each well, divide the acceptor‑channel value by the donor‑channel value to obtain the expression signal ratio [acceptor]/[donor].

steps.title: Normalize expression ratios
steps.instruction: Divide each expression signal ratio by the ratio obtained for the 1:1 A/D plasmid condition (as defined in Table 1) to get the normalized expression signal ratio.

steps.title: Plot BRET data in Prism
steps.instruction: Open GraphPad Prism, create an XY table, and plot the averaged BRET ratios (Y‑axis) against the corresponding acceptor/donor plasmid ratios (1:1 to 40:1) (X‑axis). Optionally plot expression‑signal‑ratio‑based graphs as shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

steps.title: Fit saturation binding curve
steps.instruction: In Prism, select Analyze → XY analyses → Nonlinear regression → Hyperbola (x is a concentration). Use the equation y = BRETmax × x / (BRET50 + x), where x = relative acceptor/donor expression and y = BRET ratio.

steps.title: Determine BRETtop value
steps.instruction: Duplicate the data table, choose Analyze → Fit a curve with nonlinear regression → One‑phase association, constrain Y0 = 0, and record the Plateau parameter (BRETtop) with its standard error.
